title: Mirsky's theorem (hard direction) for finite posets, connected to Set.chainHeight

problemStatement.formal: \max_{\text{chain } C}\, |C| \;=\; \min\{\, k : P = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_k,\ A_i \text{ antichains}\,\}.
problemStatement.plain: Mirsky's theorem is the order-dual of Dilworth's theorem. Its hard direction says: label each element by the length of the longest chain ending at it; elements sharing a label form an antichain, so the poset splits into exactly (longest chain length) antichains. This problem asks to formalize that construction for finite posets and connect the "longest chain length" to Mathlib's `Set.chainHeight`.
